question.text: Which valuation approach is MOST theoretically acceptable per the chapter as the primary valuation method for investee companies, with other methods used for corroboration?

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter opens with: 'the most acceptable by theoretical standards is the one that estimates the value of an asset as the present value of its future cash flows' - the DCF / NPV method. Other methods are used to corroborate. The Trap: Replacement/break-up/book are asset-based approaches - useful for distressed or asset-heavy businesses but not primary. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XXI-B echo this DCF-primacy. XV (Research Analyst) uses DCF as anchor with multiples for cross-check.
